The two perpendicular chords are each tangent to the concentric radius-6 circle, so their distances from O are 6. In the radius-10 circle each half-chord is √(10²−6²)=8. With P at chord intersection, AP=8+6=14, choice 1.

OM bisects chord AB, so AM=BM=6. With CM=3 and OM=r−3, right triangle OMB gives r²=(r−3)²+6², so r=7cm.

Rectangle height 12 gives circle radius 6 and tangent lengths from A to E/F equal 6. Given D-to-tangent length 15, AD=AE+ED=6+15=21, hence BC=21. Right triangle DHC has DH=15, DC=12, so HC=9; GH=BC−BG−HC=21−6−9=6cm.
